b: ORLANDO — Orlando is poised to become the top meetings destination in the U.S. in 2027, jumping from fourth place in 2026, according to American Express Global Business Travel’s (Amex GBT) recently released 2027 Meetings and Events Forecast.

Las Vegas ranks second, followed by Chicago, New York City and Dallas. Those four cities have maintained positions among North America’s five leading meetings destinations for three consecutive years.
Orlando’s ascent highlights the competitive advantages of destinations that combine accessibility, extensive hotel inventory and convention infrastructure.

“Orlando’s rise is driven by a combination of factors, led by accessibility and capacity,” Paul McDonnough, Senior Manager, Global Events and Account Management at Amex GBT, said. “Strong air connectivity and ease of travel make it an attractive destination, while its large hotel inventory and convention facilities can accommodate events of all sizes.”

The survey encompasses corporate meetings, conventions and trade shows, with respondents evaluating destinations based on accessibility, cost, safety, infrastructure, local attractions, attendee experience and sustainability.
Why Established Convention Markets Remain Competitive
While Orlando made the biggest move among the top five U.S. destinations, Las Vegas, Chicago, New York City and Dallas continue to demonstrate staying power.
McDonnough attributes their consistent rankings to the combination of infrastructure, accessibility and value that meeting organizers prioritize.
“These destinations have staying power because they consistently deliver what planners value most: strong hotel and meeting capacity, accessibility and competitive pricing,” McDonnough said.
Each market also offers distinct advantages.

Las Vegas benefits from its extensive hotel room inventory and air connectivity, while Chicago combines substantial convention capacity with a central location that makes it accessible to attendees traveling from across the country.
New York City offers global connectivity and entertainment options, while Dallas competes in convenient access and competitive hotel rates.

For organizers, these advantages are particularly important when evaluating destinations capable of accommodating large exhibit floors, substantial room blocks and attendees arriving from multiple markets.
The continued dominance of established convention cities also underscores the importance of infrastructure investments and accessibility in maintaining a destination’s competitive position.
Internationally, Barcelona is projected to become Europe’s leading meetings destination in 2027, overtaking London.
Madrid ranks second, followed by Paris and Lisbon.
McDonnough said Barcelona’s appeal extends beyond its meeting facilities to the overall experience it offers attendees.
“Barcelona’s rise reflects its appeal as an overall attendee experience, combining culture, food, nightlife and beach access with strong incentive travel opportunities,” McDonnough said.
London remains a formidable competitor, supported by its global connectivity, extensive venue inventory and position as an international business hub.
The rankings suggest that destinations offering compelling experiences beyond the convention center are increasingly attractive to meeting organizers.
Buenos Aires Takes the Top Spot in Latin America
Buenos Aires is projected to lead Latin America’s meetings destination rankings in 2027, followed by Mexico City, São Paulo, Panama City and Rio de Janeiro.
McDonnough pointed to the Argentinian capital’s combination of cultural attractions, culinary experiences, conference infrastructure and value for international groups.
The city’s ascent reflects the importance of destinations that can offer both business infrastructure and memorable experiences while remaining competitive on cost.
In Asia-Pacific, Singapore retains its position as the region’s leading meetings destination, followed by Bangkok, Tokyo, Seoul and Sydney.
Value and Attendee Experience Drive Site Selection
Although affordability remains a major consideration for meeting organizers, McDonnough said destination selection is becoming more nuanced.
“While controlling expenses remains a priority, rising costs are no longer viewed as the single biggest challenge heading into 2027,” McDonnough said.
Instead, organizations are weighing costs against accessibility, infrastructure and the overall attendee experience.
That shift is creating opportunities for destinations that can offer strong value without sacrificing the quality of the event.
“The biggest shift is that organizations are taking a more balanced approach to destination selection, weighing affordability against the overall attendee experience,” McDonnough said.
Planners are also expanding their searches beyond traditional markets to consider emerging destinations offering competitive pricing, convenient access and new experiences.
Safety and geopolitical considerations are becoming increasingly important in destination decisions, particularly for international events.
Another consideration is the growing interest in destinations where attendees can extend business trips for personal travel.
For organizers, the findings reinforce the importance of evaluating destinations beyond convention center capacity and hotel availability.

While established markets continue to benefit from their infrastructure and accessibility, destinations that deliver a compelling combination of value, convenience and powerful attendee experiences may be better positioned to compete for future events.
